title: The Frog at the Bottom of the Well

parts.text: Hello, little friends! If you sat at the bottom of a well your whole life and looked up, would the sky look big or small?
Long ago, there was a frog who believed the sky was only as big as a pot lid.
Today, Huy Tells Tales will tell you the fable of the Frog at the Bottom of the Well.
Once upon a time, in a village beside the Red River, there were green bamboo hedges all around, a big banyan tree, and a temple house with a curved roof.
In a corner of the village stood an old well, its walls covered in green moss. It had been a long time since anyone came there to draw water.
At the bottom of the well lived a little Frog with his friend Crab, some Snails, and a few tiny tree frogs.
Every morning, Frog hopped onto the rock in the middle of the well and called out as loudly as he could.
Ribbit! Ribbit! This morning I woke up earliest in the whole well again!
His croak bounced off the walls of the well and rang out, deep and loud, sounding very grand.
Did you hear that? My voice echoes across the whole world!
Frog, that is only the walls of the well sending your voice back.
No! It is because I am the greatest!
Frog looked up. Through the round mouth of the well, he saw only a small patch of blue sky.
The sky is only as big as a pot lid. I can see the whole sky!
Frog puffed out his chest and his cheeks, and looked down at his little friends around him.
I am the king of the whole wide world! Crab, Snails, bow to me at once!
Yes, yes, hello, your majesty.
The Snails were so frightened that they pulled their heads into their shells.
But Miss Sparrow flew by and told us that outside, it is very wide.
Lies! There is nothing outside this well at all!
Day after day, Frog only ate, slept, croaked, and bragged.
He would not listen to anyone, and he did not want to learn anything new.
Then one day, dark clouds filled the sky. Thunder rumbled, rain poured down in buckets, and the bamboo hedges swayed.
Oh my, what heavy rain!
More and more rainwater poured into the well. The water rose and rose.
The water is so high! I am being pushed up!
Frog, be careful!
The water spilled over the mouth of the well, swept Frog outside, and set him down on the wet grass beside the village road.
Oh! Where in the world am I?
The rain stopped. Frog looked around and saw that the sky today was much bigger. But he still would not believe it.
Hmph, the rain must have made the sky swell up. I am still the king!
So Frog strutted proudly out into the middle of the village road.
On the road, Ant was busily carrying a grain of rice bigger than his whole body.
Hey, you tiny creature, why don't you bow to the king?
Hello, Frog! I am busy carrying rice home to my nest, before it rains again.
What is rice? There is nothing like that in my well.
Rice grows in the fields over there! A whole field of golden rice, wide and endless!
A field? I bet it is only as big as my well!
Go and see, and you will know.
Suddenly the ground began to shake. Clip-clop, clip-clop! A brown Horse galloped down the village road as fast as the wind.
Move aside! Move aside!
Oh! What a huge creature!
Horse stopped quickly, only a tiny bit away from Frog.
I almost stepped on you. Why are you sitting in the middle of the road?
I... I am the king.
Ha ha, what kind of king is so tiny?
I just ran all the way from the river dike to the village gate. Out there, there are markets, rivers, and so many other villages too.
Really? Is the world that wide?
Just then, Uncle Buffalo came slowly home from the fields. On his back sat a little boy with a topknot, playing a flute.
Children, what is all this noise about?
Uncle, I came up from the well. I thought the sky was only as big as a pot lid, so why is it so big now?
Ha ha, sitting at the bottom of a well, you could only see a tiny patch of sky.
Come, climb onto my back, and I will take you to the fields to see.
Frog leaped onto Uncle Buffalo's back. Ant crawled up onto his horn, and Horse walked beside them.
When they reached the fields, Frog saw a whole sea of golden rice rustling in the wind. White storks fluttered by, and far away he saw the river dike and green bamboo hedges.
Wow, it is so wide! A thousand times wider than my well!
Frog looked up. The blue sky stretched on and on, white clouds drifted lazily, and the children's kites soared high.
The sky is not a pot lid at all! It is so big, I cannot see where it ends!
See? I told you so!
Frog bowed his head, and his cheeks turned red.
All this time, I thought I was the king. It turns out I know so little.
I also shouted at my friends in the well. I am so ashamed.
Knowing that you do not know is already wiser. Everyone has things they do not know, dear child. We only need to work hard and learn.
Frog turned to Ant and Horse.
I was so rude earlier. Please forgive me, my friends.
It is all right, we are friends!
Frog crossed his arms and bowed his head politely.
Uncle Buffalo, dear friends, please take me everywhere so that I can learn!
Of course! Tomorrow I will take you to the village market!
And I will show you how to find rice!

In the days after that, Frog followed his friends everywhere. He visited the busy village market, stopped by the cool village pond, admired the temple yard, and even climbed up to the windy river dike.
Today I learned something new again!
One afternoon, Frog went back to the edge of the old well and called down to his friend.
Crab, it is so wide out here! I was wrong before, and I am sorry!
How wonderful! Frog, tell me all about it!
Frog sat on Uncle Buffalo's back and watched the red sunset glow over the fields.
Thank you, Uncle Buffalo. You are my very first teacher!
Little friends, from this story, our grandparents made a saying, a frog at the bottom of a well. When someone knows little but likes to brag, people still say it to this very day.

In 2005, filmmakers used this story to make The Dream of the Green Frog, the first 3D animated film in Vietnam. The film ends with the words, Go and you will know this and that, stay in one place and you will never grow wise.
Uncle Buffalo led Frog out of his tiny sky the size of a pot lid. Your teachers do the same, every day opening a whole sky of knowledge for you.
Vietnamese Teachers Day, on the twentieth of November, is coming soon. Remember to cross your arms and thank your teachers!
This story reminds us not to be proud like Frog was in his well. The world is very wide, so let us be humble and work hard to learn every day.
If you liked today's story, please subscribe to the channel Huy Kể Chuyện to hear many more wonderful stories. See you again, friends!

cast.name: Frog
cast.role: Ếch con sống dưới đáy giếng cũ, lúc đầu tự cao cho mình là chúa tể, sau nhận ra mình biết ít và xin đi học hỏi

cast.name: Uncle Buffalo
cast.role: Bác trâu cày hiền lành, chở Ếch ra đồng, dạy Ếch bài học khiêm tốn, như người thầy đầu tiên

cast.name: Ant
cast.role: Bạn Kiến chăm chỉ tha thóc, kể cho Ếch về cánh đồng

cast.name: Horse
cast.role: Bạn Ngựa chạy nhanh, đã đi nhiều nơi, kể cho Ếch về chợ, sông, các làng

cast.name: Crab
cast.role: Bạn Cua nhỏ sống chung trong giếng, bị Ếch bắt cúi chào, sau được Ếch xin lỗi

facts.claim: Ếch ngồi đáy giếng là truyện ngụ ngôn Việt Nam, nhân vật là loài vật được nhân hóa để đưa ra bài học cho con người
Truyện phê phán thói huênh hoang đi kèm bệnh chủ quan của con người
Truyện còn nêu tác hại của óc xa rời thực tế, là bài học rút ra từ cuộc sống
Từ đáy giếng nhìn lên, trời chỉ to bằng cái vung
Ếch tự vỗ ngực cho mình là chúa tể muôn loài, coi cái giếng là giang sơn của mình
Ếch chẳng đi đâu xa ngoài cái giếng nên nhiễm thói tự cao tự đại
Phim hoạt hình Giấc mơ của Ếch Xanh (2005) phỏng theo tích ếch ngồi đáy giếng, là phim hoạt hình 3D đầu tiên của điện ảnh Việt Nam
Phim khép lại bằng câu Đi thì biết đó biết đây, ở lì một chỗ biết ngày nào khôn
Phim đoạt giải Bông sen Bạc phim xuất sắc nhất tại Liên hoan phim Việt Nam lần thứ XV năm 2006

look: Bối cảnh: làng quê đồng bằng sông Hồng thế kỷ XVII–XIX. Giếng cũ ở góc làng: thành giếng tròn xây đá ong hoặc gạch cũ, phủ rêu xanh, bên cạnh có gốc tre, đáy giếng có nước trong, hòn đá cho Ếch ngồi, rêu và lá rụng. Làng có lũy tre xanh bao quanh, cổng làng, cây đa, đình làng mái ngói cong vừa phải kiểu Bắc Bộ (không cong vút kiểu Trung Hoa), nhà tranh vách đất, sân đất, ao làng, đường làng đất nện. Cánh đồng lúa chín vàng, đàn cò trắng, đê sông xa xa, chợ quê với quang gánh, thúng mủng, nồi đất, chum vại. Nhân vật con vật vẽ kiểu hoạt hình dễ thương, không mặc quần áo: Ếch con xanh lá, mắt to tròn, bụng trắng, lúc kiêu thì ưỡn ngực phồng má, lúc biết lỗi thì cúi đầu má ửng hồng; Cua nhỏ màu nâu cam, Ốc vỏ nâu, nhái bén xanh nhạt; Kiến nhỏ màu nâu đỏ, mắt tròn tươi tắn, tha hạt thóc vàng; Ngựa nâu khỏe, bờm đen, chỉ có dây cương thừng đơn giản, không yên cương kiểu Tây; Bác Trâu đen xám to lớn, sừng cong, mắt hiền, dáng thong thả. Người trong làng chỉ làm nền: cậu bé tóc để chỏm, áo cánh ngắn nâu, quần lửng, chân đất, cưỡi lưng trâu thổi sáo trúc; trẻ em thả diều sáo trên đồng; nông dân nam áo cánh nâu, quần xắn gối, nón lá, vác cuốc; phụ nữ áo tứ thân nâu ngoài yếm, váy đen dài, thắt lưng bao, khăn mỏ quạ, nón lá, gánh thúng đi chợ. Không có đồ hiện đại, không ngô, ớt, không nón bài thơ.
